problem: Source-free single-utterance ASR adaptation under distribution shift
method: Unsupervised frame-level Shannon entropy + Minimum Class Confusion (MCC) loss on CTC layer norm parameters
main_strength: Enables test-time adaptation on single utterances without source data or acoustic labels
limitation_relevant_to_our_work: Evaluates exclusively aggregate WER on noise/domain shifts; does not evaluate continual streaming, order sensitivity, or subgroup disparity
how_our_work_differs: Evaluates continual prequential streaming across real accent groups, characterizes adaptation-induced subgroup regression, and wraps candidate updates with the DSG controller

problem: Error accumulation and catastrophic collapse during continual test-time ASR adaptation on noisy speech
method: Periodic model parameter restore / reset mechanism and EMA tracking to counteract drift
main_strength: Prevents unbounded error divergence on continuous non-stationary acoustic noise streams
limitation_relevant_to_our_work: Focuses on acoustic noise corruption without social demographic or accent group metadata; evaluates aggregate WER, leaving subgroup regression unmonitored
how_our_work_differs: Evaluates across 6 verified accent strata, demonstrates condition-dependent subgroup regression (+2.17% on severe noise), and adds multi-objective statistical risk screening

problem: Single-model plasticity-stability trade-off during continual test-time adaptation
method: Dynamic model bank retrieval: maintains multiple expert checkpoints and selects best matching model per stream segment
main_strength: Mitigates catastrophic forgetting by routing acoustic shifts to specialized model checkpoints
limitation_relevant_to_our_work: Model retrieval is vulnerable to acoustic interference (babble noise triggers severe negative transfer: +8.15% regression on Hindi); no disparity or subgroup safety constraint
how_our_work_differs: Characterizes catastrophic model retrieval failure under multi-talker babble noise and screens model updates through an independent speaker-disjoint sentinel panel

problem: Reinforcement learning for test-time ASR robustness without transcripts
method: Test-time RL using multi-modal audio-text semantic similarity rewards to guide gradient updates
main_strength: Bypasses reliance on pure unsupervised entropy minimization using semantic semantic-consistency rewards
limitation_relevant_to_our_work: Requires complex reward models and heavy compute at test time; evaluated on generic noise/perturbations without accent or equity stratification
how_our_work_differs: Operates under standard lightweight test-time updates (layer-norm/adapter tuning) while enforcing explicit statistical bounds on subgroup and disparity risk

problem: Lack of standardized fairness and equity benchmarking across commercial and open-source ASR
method: Comprehensive static benchmarking suite computing demographic parity, equal opportunity, and WER disparity metrics
dataset: Diverse multi-accent and multi-dialect corpora (Common Voice, VoxCeleb, etc.)
main_strength: Provides unified equity evaluation metrics and establishes baseline disparities across demographics
limitation_relevant_to_our_work: Purely static evaluation framework; does not investigate dynamic adaptation, continual learning, or test-time adaptation safety
how_our_work_differs: Bridges static equity benchmarking with continual test-time adaptation, measuring dynamic disparity growth (Delta_D) and worst-group regression (max_g Delta_g) during inference

paper: Responsible Benchmarking of Fairness for ASR (SPEAKABLE)
problem: Methodological flaws and confounding variables in speech recognition fairness evaluations
method: Controlled demographic stratification protocols adjusting for acoustic SNR, speaking rate, and recording channel confounds
main_strength: Highlights that raw demographic disparities often conflate acoustic recording artifacts with phonetic bias; advocates GLMM and confounder control
limitation_relevant_to_our_work: Focuses on benchmark design and static evaluation guidelines; does not propose online adaptation algorithms or safety intervention mechanisms
how_our_work_differs: Adopts SPEAKABLE recommendations by performing Poisson GLMM confounder control in Stage 2, then extends the methodology into a real-time statistical safety gate (DSG)

problem: Lack of conversational, diverse international accent corpora for ASR evaluation
method: 40-hour conversational English corpus covering 40 global accents, recorded remotely via video calls
dataset: EdAcc corpus (Edinburgh International Accents of English)
main_strength: Captures naturalistic, non-native conversational speech across wide linguistic backgrounds
limitation_relevant_to_our_work: Highly unbalanced speaker distribution and subjective self-reported accents; conversational overlap prevents clean speaker-disjoint streaming evaluation
how_our_work_differs: Uses balanced scripted speech (L2-ARCTIC and Common Voice 27.0) with strict 10-speaker/group balance to enforce mathematically rigorous speaker-disjoint prequential streaming

problem: Catastrophic forgetting during continual domain expansion in speech recognition
method: Parameter-efficient adapters (LoRA, prefix-tuning) updated sequentially with replay buffers or regularization
main_strength: Achieves parameter-efficient adaptation with minimal memory overhead during continual learning
limitation_relevant_to_our_work: Requires supervised training with ground-truth transcripts; does not address unsupervised test-time adaptation or demographic subgroup fairness
how_our_work_differs: Addresses fully source-free, unsupervised test-time adaptation without reference transcripts, enforcing statistical subgroup risk constraints via an air-gapped sentinel panel
